meta.title: The Bean Jar
meta.textType: functional: steps and a labeled diagram in an email

paragraphs: On Tuesday, January fifth, Lily brought an email from her pen pal Grace to class. Teacher Kim, Lily, and Leo stood beside the laptop. Grace wrote, "Dear Lily, we grew beans in jars in our class." "Here are the steps, and here is my diagram." The diagram showed the seed on day one and the root on day four. Then it showed the shoot on day seven and the first leaves on day ten. An arrow with the word "water" pointed to the jar. "Can we grow beans, too?" asked Leo.

Teacher Kim read the steps slowly, and the class followed them. "Step one: wet a paper towel." "Step two: put it in a clear jar." "Step three: push three beans between the towel and the glass." "Step four: cover the top of the jar with a cloth." "Step five: put the jar near a window." "Step six: add a little water every day." Mia poured a little water from a small cup. May held up a label, and Lily wrote "Day one" on it. Leo asked, "Will a bean grow in the dark?" "If you keep the jar in a cupboard, the shoot will be yellow and thin," said Teacher Kim. "If you put it near a window, it will become green."

Six days later, on day seven, the seeds became green shoots. Teacher Kim gave Leo a record sheet. It had two words at the top: "Day" and "Height." Leo held a ruler beside the tallest jar. "The shoot is six centimeters tall," he said. Lily wrote three lines in the record. "Day one: seed." "Day four: root, two centimeters." "Day seven: shoot, six centimeters." "If we measure every day, we will have a good record," said Lily.

On day ten, the first leaves opened. The warm sun came through the window, and the plants grew toward the light. The roots went deep into the towel. May touched a leaf with one finger. "It is soft," she said. "Now the plants are ready for the school garden," said Teacher Kim. "If we plant them in the soil, they will grow big."

That evening, Lily wrote to Grace. "Dear Grace, thank you for the steps and the diagram." "In the beginning, our beans were small and hard." "Now they have green leaves." "Do your plants have leaves, too?" "Best wishes, Lily."

images.prompt: A laptop stands on a classroom desk. An arrow with the label "water" points to a jar. Teacher Kim, Lily, and Leo stand beside the desk and look at the screen.
